chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan ibn Ibrahim al-Hamdani, raised it to one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).
He said: 'I love for the man that there be a debt upon him, intending its repayment.'

key_terms.الصَّادِقِينَ: The Truthful Ones (title for the 5th and 6th Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of having a debt according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Imam (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual merit of carrying debt with the sincere intention of repayment, framing financial obligation not merely as a burden but as a means of cultivating discipline and accountability. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the moral dimension of transactions, where the intent (niyyah) transforms a worldly duty into an act of worship. The narration underscores that the struggle to fulfill one's dues is valued by God, encouraging believers to view debt as an opportunity for spiritual growth rather than solely as a financial liability.
